agent.scenario.camera.title: Camera Preview
agent.scenario.camera.desc: Detect a camera and show its image here
agent.scenario.camera.prompt: Use the configured Jetson and the supplied SSH bridge to enumerate /dev/video* and identify a usable capture source. Start the in-app preview using the camera command with the confirmed source. Reuse existing drivers and OpenCV; if missing, report the dependency. For CSI, use the actual working GStreamer pipeline. Publish camera source and capture status to the data panel.
agent.scenario.radar.title: Radar / Sensors
agent.scenario.radar.desc: Wire up lidar / radar / IMU sensors and verify data streams
agent.scenario.radar.prompt: Use the configured Jetson and supplied SSH bridge to identify serial/USB sensors and their existing driver or ROS topic. Reuse the existing reader, verify actual samples and publish scalar readings with units to the data panel. Do not invent readings or install a new stack before checking the current setup.
agent.scenario.arm.title: Robot Arm Actions
agent.scenario.arm.desc: Match the arm skill to your requested action
agent.scenario.arm.prompt: Prepare to control the robot arm on my configured Jetson. Identify the actual arm and its current state, then use the matching supplied skill and existing controller. Publish state and joint readings to the data panel. Ask me for the desired target/action if none is specified; do not run a calibration, home or movement demo by default. Execute only my requested action using the verified calibration and limits, then report measured results.

agent.scenario.ssh.title: Connect Jetson
agent.scenario.ssh.desc: Use the saved device and login settings
agent.scenario.ssh.prompt: Connect to the Jetson configured in DevelopTool using the provided connect command. Reuse its saved credentials, then verify hostname, JetPack and network addresses over the SSH bridge. Publish the measured device information to the data panel.
agent.scenario.network.title: Internet Sharing
agent.scenario.network.desc: Open the existing PC-to-Jetson sharing tool
agent.scenario.network.prompt: Help my configured Jetson access the internet through this PC. Use the supplied network command to open DevelopTool’s network-sharing panel with the current device. Reuse that tool for setup, then verify gateway, public IP, DNS and HTTPS on the Jetson using the SSH bridge. Publish the observed results. Opening the panel alone does not mean sharing is enabled.
agent.scenario.arm_read.title: Read Robot Arm
agent.scenario.arm_read.desc: Read actual joints and status without moving
agent.scenario.arm_read.prompt: Read the robot arm connected to my configured Jetson. First identify its actual model, serial/CAN connection and existing controller. Select only the matching supplied skill (SO-ARM or reBot). Read joint positions, gripper and stop state through the existing controller without moving, calibrating, disabling torque or opening a second bus owner. Publish measured values with units and their source to the data panel; explicitly mark unavailable readings.

agent.context.runtime:
[DevelopTool task context — refreshed for this turn]
Task route: {task}
Configured Jetson (public metadata only): {target}
Local PC command prefix: {helper}
Run this prefix followed by:
- status: inspect the bound device and execution permissions.
- connect: reuse DevelopTool’s saved SSH credentials (no passwords in prompts).
- ssh --command 'REMOTE COMMAND' --timeout 30: execute ON THE JETSON through DevelopTool. This preserves its SSH port, authentication and sudo setup; do not run device commands on the PC or request credentials again.
- camera start --source /dev/video0 (also supports a confirmed RTSP URL or GStreamer pipeline); camera stop: preview inside DevelopTool. Requires python3 and cv2 on the Jetson. Reuse an existing camera controller when one already owns the device.
- monitor start / monitor stop: show system readings in the data panel.
- publish --source arm --json '{{"joint_1_deg": 12.5, "stop_state": "measured state"}}': send actual measured scalar readings with units to the data panel. The example values are illustrative, never publish them as measurements. Repeat after fresh observations; do not claim a single snapshot is a continuous stream.
- network: open DevelopTool’s existing sharing panel; it returns queued, not sharing success. The user completes the panel’s configuration. Verify networking afterwards through SSH.
If disconnected, run connect first. If no host is configured, direct the user to Remote Dev. Auto-execute must be enabled for bridge connect/ssh. A changed device invalidates the old runtime. A queued visual request only confirms delivery; do not claim successful frames or measurements without evidence.
Read only these pre-matched skill files initially (choose the skill for the actual arm model):
{skills}
Prefer these fixed paths and commands over global skill searches, scanning configuration files or reinstalling working dependencies. If a named hardware skill is only on the Jetson, check only its known skill directories. Use the live controller/schema and report missing capabilities. Keep control sessions alive when holding a load; reading state does not authorize motion.
